s: Microbes are far too small for the eye. A surface can look spotless and still carry them.
cap: Why can't we see contamination? Microbes are far too small for the eye, so a surface can look spotless and still carry them. Argus detects microbial contamination invisible to the human eye.

s: Some materials absorb ultraviolet light and re-emit it as visible light. That glow can reveal what white light misses.
cap: UV fluorescence: some materials absorb ultraviolet light and re-emit it as visible light. That glow can reveal what white light misses. It's the first layer in Argus.

s: Software that reads images and turns what it sees into measurements.
cap: Optical computer vision is software that reads images and turns what it sees into measurements. In Argus it works on what UV fluorescence reveals.

s: How long a model takes to produce a result from one input. Argus states 15 ms on its profile.
cap: Inference time is how long a model takes to produce a result from one input. Argus states 15 ms inference on its profile. Fast results are what make checking practical.

s: Of everything a model flags, the share that is correct. Argus states 99.4% precision on its profile.
cap: Precision: of everything a model flags, the share that is correct. Argus states 99.4% precision on its profile. In plain terms, about 994 of every 1,000 flags would be right.

items: Looks clean|What the eye can confirm.
Is clean|What a measurement can confirm.
cap: Looks clean is what the eye can confirm. Is clean is what a measurement can confirm. They're not the same thing, and the gap is invisible by definition.

s: UV fluorescence + optical CV + biomedical AI.
cap: Three layers, one pipeline: UV fluorescence, optical computer vision and biomedical AI, working together to detect microbial contamination invisible to the human eye.

Our view: visible is a low bar. If the only test for clean is what the eye can see, we're missing the part that matters.

h: Clean should be measured, not assumed.

cap: Our view: you can't manage what you can't see. Making the invisible visible is the first step. Everything else follows.
